healthSystem: The University of Kansas Health System

financials.source: Bond Buyer reporting on $415M bond offering (2026): total revenue $5.4B in FY2025 (up from $4.5B in FY2024), total assets $5.1B; health system FY2025 financial overview confirms total operating revenue of $5,394,325 (in thousands); Q1 FY2025 Becker's report: long-term debt $1B as of Sept. 30, 2024; the University of Kansas Hospital Authority is a state instrumentality created by K.S.A. 76-3304 and does not file Form 990

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Not separately disclosed in public financial overviews; S&P noted days cash on hand of 154 days in FY2025, down from 161 days in FY2023 and FY2024; balance sheet figures described as 'relatively weak compared with peers' by S&P Global
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Total assets of $5.1B against long-term debt of $1B as of Sept. 30, 2024, implying net assets in the range of $3B-$4B depending on other liabilities. The system does not publish a detailed balance sheet in its publicly available financial overviews. Its audited financial statements and bond investor presentations contain the full breakdown but are not freely available online. The $415M bond offering in 2026 — its first new debt since 2019 — will increase total leverage significantly.

bondDebt.source: Bond Buyer 2026: $415M offering split into $365M fixed-rate and $50M put bonds, secured by gross revenue pledge, rated AA- by both Fitch and S&P; proceeds fund cancer pavilion, purchase of leased Indian Creek Campus buildings, and refunding of 2004, 2011, and 2015 series; Becker's Hospital Review Q1 FY2025: long-term debt was $1B as of Sept. 30, 2024; this was the first debt issuance since 2019

otherRelatedEntities: University of Kansas Medical Center Research Institute (EIN 48-1108830)
relatedOrganizations.source: HRSA 340B database; ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer; Daffy.org; Kansas University Physicians Inc stated mission is 'support to the University of Kansas Hospital Authority in connection with its health care operations'; the Hospital Authority is governed by a 19-member board, 13 appointed by the Kansas governor

executiveComp.source: Bob Page has served as President and CEO since July 2007, selected by the Hospital Authority Board; the University of Kansas Hospital Authority is a state instrumentality under K.S.A. 76-3304 and does not file IRS Form 990, so executive compensation is not publicly reported through that mechanism; employees are explicitly not state employees per Kansas statute, complicating public salary disclosure; no compensation figures found in public databases

communityBenefit.source: KU Health System FY2025 Financial Overview: total community care support of $713.7M comprising $166.2M in charity care, in-kind health services, community education and advocacy, and health education training plus $547.5M in Medicaid and Medicare losses; excludes Olathe Hospital and Paola Hospital; FY2024 total was $693M ($151.1M charity care plus $541.9M Medicaid/Medicare losses); financial assistance eligibility covers patients with gross family income from 0% to 300% of federal poverty guidelines

taxAdvantage.notes: The Hospital Authority is exempt from Kansas ad valorem (property) taxes and state sales/use taxes on purchases for public purposes under K.S.A. 76-3313; its $415M in new tax-exempt bonds (2026) and prior outstanding debt generate substantial federal interest subsidy; the CVS lawsuit alleges $62M in 340B savings were diverted between 2020 and 2025, suggesting significant annual 340B program participation; specific foregone tax amounts not verified

layoffs.notes: The St. Francis Campus in Topeka eliminated 29 positions and furloughed 235 full- and part-time workers during COVID-19 pandemic restructuring; CEO framed cuts as consolidation of some services; no other hospitals in the system were reported affected

keyRiskFactors: S&P assigned negative outlook citing weak days cash on hand — slipped from 161 days in FY2023/FY2024 to 154 days in FY2025
S&P noted balance sheet figures remain 'relatively weak compared with peers'
$415M new bond offering in 2026, first debt issuance since 2019, will significantly increase leverage atop $1B existing long-term debt
Rapid acquisition pace: absorbed Olathe Health (2023) and Liberty Hospital (2024) while still integrating operations
Thin operating margins — Q1 FY2025 margin of 2.2% ($26.8M on $1.22B revenue), following a -1.5% loss in Q1 FY2024

program340B.notes: Registered as DSH170040 (Disproportionate Share Hospital) since 10/1/2000; HRSA database shows multiple contract pharmacies including specialty pharmacies (Caremark, Accredo Health Group, Onco360); CVS terminated its contract pharmacy arrangement with KU in 2025 after the hospital requested an audit; the Hospital Authority filed suit in May 2026 alleging CVS diverted approximately $62M in 340B savings between 2020 and 2025

acquisitions.notes: Two-hospital system in Olathe, Kansas; deal finalized January 2023; included commitments to bring KU Cancer Center care to Olathe campus and support Magnet nursing designation; Fitch cited the acquisition as contributing to improved scale

First hospital acquisition in Missouri; letter of intent signed November 2023, deal closed July 1, 2024; KU Health System pledged $324M investment in Liberty's service area and guaranteed no layoffs for at least one year; deal drew legislative opposition from Missouri lawmakers who pre-filed bills to block it; Liberty Hospital Foundation remains a separate entity

lobbying.source: Not verified; as a state instrumentality the Hospital Authority may have different disclosure requirements than a private nonprofit

legalIssues.description: University of Kansas Hospital Authority sued CVS and subsidiaries alleging CVS diverted approximately $62M in 340B drug pricing savings between 2020 and 2025; KU claims CVS terminated the contract pharmacy arrangement in retaliation after the hospital requested an audit of CVS records

KCUR/The Beacon investigation found the University of Kansas Health System and NKC Health are the only Kansas City area hospitals that garnish patients' wages; the system had sued more than 400 patients in Missouri and Kansas in 2026 alone (approximately 218 cases in Missouri, 114 in Kansas); other area systems including St. Luke's and AdventHealth do not sue patients, garnish wages, or place liens

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Investment portfolio not separately disclosed; operating income not reported for full FY2025; Q1 FY2025 operating income was $26.8M (2.2% margin) on $1.22B revenue
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Existing $1B long-term debt (Sept. 2024) against $713.7M claimed community benefit (FY2025) yields a ratio of 1.4x; with the $415M new issuance, total debt could approach $1.4B, pushing the ratio toward 2.0x — meaning every dollar of claimed community benefit would be matched by nearly two dollars of tax-exempt debt
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Charity care of $166.2M against $5.4B total revenue is approximately 3.1% of revenue; the bulk of the system's $713.7M community benefit claim ($547.5M, or 77%) consists of Medicaid and Medicare shortfalls rather than charity care

accusation: Sits atop $5.1 billion in total assets with $5.4 billion in annual revenue as a tax-exempt state instrumentality, yet garnishes the wages of patients who cannot pay their medical bills — one of only two hospitals in Kansas City that does so — while suing more than 400 patients in a single year. Issued $415 million in new tax-exempt bonds in 2026 atop $1 billion in existing debt, even as S&P downgraded its outlook to negative over weakening cash reserves. Claims $713.7 million in community benefit, but 77% of that figure ($547.5 million) is Medicaid and Medicare shortfalls rather than actual charity care. Meanwhile, alleges CVS diverted $62 million in 340B drug pricing savings — taxpayer-subsidized discounts intended for vulnerable patients — raising questions about oversight of its own contract pharmacy operations.
